I am an old woman here in Mulanje, and this small piece of land must feed my family. The fertilizer from the government subsidy helps me, but it is never enough, so I stretch it with the manure from my goats and some compost. I plant the hybrid maize seed when I can get it from the subsidy, and I intercrop with pigeon peas and pumpkins like my mother taught me. I cannot afford pesticides or to hire many people — my children and grandchildren help me weed, and I work the hoe myself from morning until the sun is high.
